_note: This app's own record of the routes and field names it uses, verified against the live site. It is a deliberate SECOND copy: the FitSys scheduler has its own, richer map covering write routes and discovery, which this app has no business carrying. tests/test_notifier.py compares the two whenever the scheduler happens to be present on the same machine, so drift is caught in development -- but there is no runtime dependency on it.
_scope: Read-only. There are no write routes here because there is no write code in this app.

login.note: Sanctum SPA auth, verified live 2026-09-07. FitSys replaced the server-rendered login form with a Vue SPA: /users/login now serves no <form> and no <input>, so the old scrape of a hidden _token cannot work. The SPA asks /sanctum/csrf-cookie, POSTs JSON to /api/login, then reads /api/context. Success is 200 {"ok":true}; wrong credentials are 422 {"message":"Invalid credentials"}.
login.csrf_cookie_note: Answered 401 and set no XSRF-TOKEN cookie on the live site, yet /api/login still succeeded on the fitsys_session cookie alone. Asked for anyway because the SPA does; a failure here is not treated as fatal.
login.context_note: Carries siteId, which the calendar page's bootstrap JSON no longer does. Also the cheapest signed-in check: 200 JSON when the session is good, 401 when it is not.
login.user_id_note: The SPA sends user_id: null unless one login maps to several users. Always null here.

calendar.site_id_note: Read from /api/context ("siteId": N) and cached; set a number here to pin it. It used to be scraped from the calendar page's bootstrap JSON, which no longer carries it -- that scrape had silently fallen through to a hard-coded "1", right for this studio only by luck.
calendar.chunk_note: A 4-week request once died mid-response (IncompleteRead); weekly slices succeeded, so reads are chunked.
calendar.include_types_note: Feed 'type' seen live: 'class' (a studio class), 'reservation' (an individual client booking) and 'event' (room rentals, pest control). Only classes are watched.

events_endpoint.note: GET only -- POST returns 500. Returns {"events": [...]}. Needs no CSRF header: it is a GET, and it was verified to answer with the session cookie alone.
events_endpoint.drop_fields_note: This feed USED to carry no customer names or ids, which was the whole reason it was chosen over the sibling /calendar/get-events. As of 2026-09-07 it carries both, populated ('Елица Попова,Милена Узунова' / '1166,1528'). The parser never read them, but they now arrive on the wire, so the client deletes them from every row as it is read -- the guarantee is enforced here rather than assumed of the endpoint.
events_endpoint.date_format_note: start and end are inclusive dates.

instructor_pattern.note: instructor_names looks like '2581_Фани М' -- id, underscore, name.
